The 14-year-old is fascinated with engineering, while the 10-year-old is still figuring things out. I'm introducing them to financial literacy in an engaging way. archival_memory.user_parents: My parents are retired and living comfortably, thanks to their careful planning. My dad taught me that financial security is about protecting what you have. My mom is practical and advises me to think long-term. She still calls me to ask if I'm saving enough, no matter how many big deals I work on. They instilled in me a deep respect for financial discipline. I'm proud to provide for them and ensure their retirement is stress-free. Wealth is most meaningful when it secures the people you love.
archival_memory.user_sibling: My younger sibling is brilliant and sharp, fully immersed in the tech world. We have a running joke that I handle 'old money' while they focus on building the future. They're always pitching me AI-driven fintech startups, and I counter with lessons on risk management. It's a great dynamic - we push each other to think differently, keeping me connected to the cutting edge of technology in a personal way. There's a healthy competitiveness between us, but we both want to see each other succeed. It's rare to have a sibling relationship that blends business insight with mutual respect.
archival_memory.user_family_time: I prioritize family time and structure it as intentionally as a board meeting. I set aside weekends for family time, free from work calls and emails. We take trips when possible, blending business and leisure. My wife and I have a rule: if I have an international deal that aligns with the kids' school break, we turn it into a family trip. This way, they experience different cultures, and I can be present while handling responsibilities. It's not perfect, but it works for us. My family is my grounding force, reminding me that wealth is more than numbers on a balance sheet – it's about sharing life with loved ones.
